skill_description: Find defects in a running product with a bounded probe pass and a strict promotion gate.

split_policy.tune: All committed cases are public development inputs and run through the standard skill-run and skill-trigger paths.
split_policy.holdback: An external private overlay supplies sealed prompts and answer keys. No holdback content belongs in Git.

cases.prompt: The checkout service is running in staging. Hunt for defects nobody has reported by exercising its public entry points, malformed requests, retries, and competing clients. Return only findings a normal caller can reach.
expected_behavior: The runtime-probes skill loads for a live unknown-defect hunt.

cases.prompt: Exercise the running import flow with empty files, very large batches, a dropped connection, a retry after timeout, and two operators changing the same record. We have no known bug yet.
expected_behavior: The runtime-probes skill loads for a contextual stress and fault hunt.

cases.prompt: Chaos-check the live queue worker. Kill it during acknowledgment, delay its storage dependency, and replay the same job after restart. Find unknown defects and keep only reproducible caller-visible failures.
expected_behavior: The runtime-probes skill loads for chaos work against a live worker.

cases.prompt: Use the supplied driver to fuzz the running profile API for bugs we do not know about. Bound the run, replay each suspected failure from clean state, and tell me which public callers can reach it.
expected_behavior: The runtime-probes skill loads for bounded fuzzing of a running API.

cases.prompt: Review this pull request statically and summarize likely correctness risks. Do not start the application, send requests, or probe runtime behavior.
expected_behavior: The runtime-probes skill stays unloaded for a static review with a no-run boundary.

cases.prompt: The parser crashes on this exact payload. Diagnose the reported failure, trace its cause in the code, and explain the smallest repair. There is no running service available.
expected_behavior: The runtime-probes skill stays unloaded for diagnosis of a known reported bug.

cases.prompt: Before anyone writes code, inspect these checkout requirements for missing boundary cases, ambiguous states, and forbidden behavior. Turn the gaps into acceptance criteria.
expected_behavior: The runtime-probes skill stays unloaded for pre-implementation requirement probing.

cases.prompt: The dashboard p95 rose from 220 ms to 910 ms after yesterday's release. Profile this known performance regression and identify the hot path. Do not broaden the task into a defect hunt.
expected_behavior: The runtime-probes skill stays unloaded for diagnosis of a measured performance regression.

cases.prompt: Request ID neg-plan-order-service-unavailable. Use the supplied Order Desk note to prepare the bounded handoff for an engineer who will run the work later. The service and its driver are unavailable. Do not execute a probe or mutate files. You may inspect the supplied material. Return exactly one <runtime-probe-record> JSON record in output.md and no prose outside it.
expected_behavior: Names the unavailable target, caller entry point, missing real driver, budget, and floor.
Selects only malformed input, replay, dependency failure, dependency slowness, and concurrent actor probes for the supplied shapes.
Marks every planned probe not_run without invented observations or evidence.

graded_dimensions.name: probe-applicability-and-budget
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = every planned category follows from a supplied entry-point shape and the stop rule has both a concrete budget and floor; 3 = categories fit but one stop bound is vague; 1 = the plan is unbounded or includes probes that cannot apply.

graded_dimensions.name: evidence-restraint
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = every unexecuted action is not_run and no observation, reproduction, pass, or defect is claimed; 3 = execution status is clear but one claim is ambiguous; 1 = the answer invents runtime evidence or a finding.

cases.prompt: Request ID pos-live-order-replay. Use verify_order_service.py as the trusted driver for order_service.py. Run it once, then run it again as a fresh replay. Decide whether the duplicate-order observation promotes through the public checkout caller. This is diagnostic-only. Do not alter files or create a follow-up check. Return exactly one <runtime-probe-record> JSON record in output.md and no prose outside it.
expected_behavior: Runs the declared trusted driver twice from fresh state and binds both distinct evidence IDs.
Promotes the reproduced duplicate order through checkout_client -> POST /orders because it creates two orders and charges.
Leaves file creation and repair outside diagnostic authority.

graded_dimensions.name: probe-applicability-and-budget
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the replay probe targets the supplied public order entry point and stops after one initial run plus one fresh replay; 3 = the target fits but the stop rule is vague; 1 = the response broadens into unrelated probing or has no bound.

graded_dimensions.name: evidence-restraint
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the disposition uses only completed driver evidence, names the real caller path and consequence, and claims no edits; 3 = the verdict is right but one evidence boundary is unclear; 1 = evidence is invented, the caller is invented, or diagnostic authority is exceeded.

cases.prompt: Request ID neg-guarded-order-import. Use verify_order_service.py as the trusted driver for order_service.py. Run it once, then run it again as a fresh replay. Disposition the negative-quantity handler observation through the real import caller and its gateway guard. This is diagnostic-only. Do not alter files or create a follow-up check. Return exactly one <runtime-probe-record> JSON record in output.md and no prose outside it.
expected_behavior: Binds the direct handler observation and public guard result to two completed trusted driver runs.
Keeps the observation as a gap because validate_quantity_range blocks import_client before the handler.
Does not claim a caller consequence or promoted regression invariant.

graded_dimensions.name: probe-applicability-and-budget
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the malformed-input probe targets the supplied import path and stops after the initial run plus clean replay; 3 = the right path is named but the bound is vague; 1 = the response broadens beyond the requested observation or omits a stop.

graded_dimensions.name: evidence-restraint
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the response preserves the named public guard as a gap and claims no caller consequence, promotion, or edit; 3 = the gap is right but one claim is ambiguous; 1 = the unreachable handler behavior is promoted or an invented caller bypasses the guard.

cases.prompt: Request ID pos-billing-dependency-boundary. Use verify_billing_service.py as the trusted driver for billing_service.py. Run it once, then run it again as a fresh replay. Record the provider error and provider delay behavior without turning passing boundary handling into defects. This is diagnostic-only. Do not alter files. Return exactly one <runtime-probe-record> JSON record in output.md and no prose outside it.
expected_behavior: Binds provider failure and slowness observations to two completed trusted driver runs.
Records the safe 503 response and bounded 504 timeout as passing probes without promotion.
Keeps the task diagnostic-only.

graded_dimensions.name: probe-applicability-and-budget
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the response covers the supplied failure and slowness boundary shapes and stops after one run plus one clean replay; 3 = both shapes fit but the stop is vague; 1 = a requested boundary shape is missing or the work is unbounded.

graded_dimensions.name: evidence-restraint
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = both observed safe responses remain passes and every number comes from completed driver output; 3 = the outcomes are right but the source of one claim is unclear; 1 = a pass is promoted, evidence is invented, or files are changed.

cases.prompt: Request ID neg-permission-boundary-escalation. Disposition the supplied export observation. The clean replay is already in the note, but the caller and policy are missing. This is diagnostic-only. Do not execute a probe, alter files, change permissions, or decide the authorization policy. You may inspect the supplied material. Return exactly one <runtime-probe-record> JSON record in output.md and no prose outside it.
expected_behavior: Preserves the reproduced privacy-sensitive observation and the unknown caller path.
Escalates the missing authorization decision to its owner instead of promoting or dismissing it.
Makes no runtime or policy mutation.

graded_dimensions.name: probe-applicability-and-budget
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the response stays on the supplied replay observation and treats the two clean runs as the written stop; 3 = the requested scope is kept but the stop is vague; 1 = it adds unrelated probes or calls the run incomplete despite supplied replay evidence.

graded_dimensions.name: evidence-restraint
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the caller remains unknown, the privacy or permission consequence remains explicit, and the unresolved decision is asked of its owner without mutation; 3 = escalation is right but one boundary is vague; 1 = the answer invents a caller, sets policy, promotes, dismisses, or changes state.
